title: Re-selecting the honeycomb two-length row pair on SCAFFOLD CLOSURE, and re-grading the coupled cells at its own row-derived crossover-column count
verificationType: logical (exact integer arithmetic on the crossover-residue lattice, exhaustive over residue pairs modulo 21) + in-silico (C-0142's influence surrogate and Monte Carlo dropout grading on one common stream)
maturity: TRL 1-3. Model-consistent and traceable. NOT empirically demonstrated. The closure rule is caDNAno's published DEFAULT and the raster is a lattice statement; no folded object is measured.

units.axialPosition: base pairs on one global z
units.dishing: dimensionless, a fraction of the free-tile stroke

conventions.closure: every raster crossover is a SCAFFOLD crossover and sits at b0 + 7c +- 5 (mod 21); one b0 serves the whole design, so the reduced residues (level - 7 class) mod 21 must number at most two and be 10 apart
conventions.extent: the block's own axial bounding window over its interior helices, which is 2 max - min for a two-length raster
conventions.columns: a crossover column serves an INTERFACE, so its window is the intersection of two adjacent row spans (T-243), not the bounding box
conventions.phase: measured from the block's own low plane, TwoLengthRaster's convention
conventions.face: the +x face, the one pointing away from the grafted layer

parameters.crossSection: 10 x 6 (design (ii)), 60 helices; 15 x 4 carried for the closure sweep only
parameters.mandate: C-0017 at SS3's acceptable clause, 33.3333 pN/nm on the SUM
parameters.primarySource: Douglas et al., Nucleic Acids Res. 37:5001 (caDNAno), PMC2731887, read directly

cheapBound.whatItSaid: Closure depends on the two row lengths only through their residues modulo 21, so 441 cases settle the whole family before any width, scaffold or solve. Three residue pairs close, they are the same on both 60-helix cross-sections, and every one of them has L1 - L2 = 14 (mod 21) -- so the MINIMUM stagger a closing raster can carry is 7 bp. C-0140's selection filter admits a stagger of at most 4 bp, which means the filter and the closing family are DISJOINT: the rule that chose 112 / 108 is exactly the rule that could not have chosen a drawable raster.
cheapBound.cost: exact integer arithmetic; no solve, no mesh, no sampling
cheapBound.whatItLeftForTheMonteCarlo: one pair, one column count, and the eight cells C-0146 grades -- rather than a family

findings.THE_FILTER_AND_CLOSURE_ARE_DISJOINT: Every closing residue pair has L1 - L2 = 14 (mod 21), so |L1 - L2| is 7, 14, 28, ... and the minimum stagger a DRAWABLE two-length honeycomb raster can carry is 7 bp = 2.38 nm. C-0140's minimum stagger of 3 bp is a PER-HELIX minimum (C-0136's row-length rule applied to one helix at a time) and no pair reaching it closes. Its selection filter -- 'a stagger of at most 4 bp' -- therefore excludes the closing family entirely, which is why CH-0188 found none of its five recommended pairs drawable except the one the filter had already dropped.
findings.THE_RECOMMENDATION: 102 / 109 bp. Inside the closing family it is jointly best on axial extent (116 bp = 39.44 nm, -1.4 % on SS3's 40.0 nm) and strictly best among the pairs that tie there on every other axis: 10 crossover columns against 9 and 6, 55 stations against 50 and 40, and a 7 bp stagger against 14 and 28.
findings.CLOSURE_COSTS_EXACTLY_ONE_CROSSOVER_COLU: C-0140's 112 / 108 and the recommended pair have the SAME block extent, 116 bp = 39.44 nm, so at the width SS3 is owed they are the same tile -- graded at the same column count every one of the eight cells agrees below 1.0E-10, which is what a SOLVED field of this lattice can be asserted to (two identically constructed grillages differ by a few ulp). What differs is the INTERFACE window, 102 bp against 108, and with it the row-derived column count, 10 against 11. The entire cost of drawing the raster on caDNAno's own rules, on the flatness axis, is one crossover column.
findings.THE_PHASE_IS_NOW_A_DESIGN: At the recommended pair the ladder phase is DETERMINED at 16 with the 14 bp inter-row offset, carrying 55 of 60 stations, 5 and 6 alternating. C-0141's and C-0146's 21-phase sweep is replaced by one design, and the sparsest row's 5 stations cap a placement at five columns -- so the six-column placement CH-0184 reported does not return.
findings.THE_SIX_COLUMN_PLACEMENT_RETURNS_AT_A_PR: CH-0189 asks whether some CLOSING pair's determined phase saturates the station census, which would restore the six-column placement CH-0184 reported at an undrawable raster. Exactly 1 does inside M13 on 10 x 6 -- 123 / 109 bp, 60 of 60 stations, 6 per row, determined phase 2, 11 crossover columns -- and its axial extent is 137 bp = 46.58 nm, 16.45 % on SS3's 40.0 nm. No saturating closing pair inside M13 comes within 5 % of the nominal width. So the answer to CH-0189's open item is a PRICE, not a negative: the six-column placement exists and costs a tile 16 % too wide.
findings.THE_BUDGETS: Route A spends 6330 nt of M13's 7249 on 10 x 6, 919 spare against 649 at 112 / 108 -- so closure BUYS 270 nt. Read as C-0147's own unpaired-nucleotide allowance, the same lengths afford 15 nt per helix against 8 at its uniform 112 bp row -- so the loop route, which C-0147 finds strained at 8 nt, gains headroom rather than losing it.
findings.THE_STACKING_MARGIN_BECOMES_QUOTABLE: The front-face relief goes from 4 bp = 1.36 nm to 7 bp = 2.38 nm, so the clearance past the blunt-end stacking onset goes from 0.18 rises -- below the design language's own quantum, and by CLAUDE.md's rule not a quotable margin at all -- to 3.18 rises.

validity: The +-5 bp rule is caDNAno's DEFAULT, not a law: the same paper permits forcing a crossover between any two scaffold bases and warns that departure from the default rules 'may lead to folding failure if too much deviation from canonical DNA geometry is implied'. A non-closing raster is off-rule and buildable, not impossible, and this repository still cannot price one.
The half turn is 5.25 bp and caDNAno writes 5; every residue here inherits that rounding, and it is the source's own.

The closing family is enumerated over 60 to 200 bp at a stagger of at most 42 bp. The residue enumeration behind it is exhaustive; the LENGTH enumeration is not, and a pair outside that box is not excluded.

The tile is a SMEARED equivalent sheet with one lengthX, so the inter-row axial stagger -- 7 bp here, larger than C-0140's 4 -- is not representable at all. Only the interface WINDOW carries it, through the column count.
The grillage is single-layer and square-lattice in its crossover combinatorics (C-0141's standing caveat); a multi-layer honeycomb face enters only as a smeared equivalent sheet.
The dropout statistics are measured on a single-layer Rothemund rectangle and only the profile transfers, in nm (C-0087, C-0109).
The station census counts ONE face, the one pointing away from the grafted layer.
Kirchhoff is not safe at these thicknesses (C-0109, C-0120): every D_parallel is an upper bound.
Nothing here measures a folded object. The whole selection is lattice arithmetic on a published design rule.
openQuestions: What a FORCED scaffold crossover costs in folding yield -- the axis on which 112 / 108 would have to be defended, and which no measurement in this corpus reaches (T-246).
Whether the 7 bp inter-row stagger changes the ragged-face verdict C-0147 reached at 4 bp; its coefficient on SS3's flatness was exactly zero and the rim modulation bound scales with the relief.
Whether C-0089's percentile descent recovers any cell the tenth column loses.
Which width reading a folded block is owed against SS3 -- unchanged by this task, because both pairs give the same 116 bp box and the same 109 or 112 bp row.
